headline: Advanced data center zoning changes toward a second reading; adopted Riverwalk North contract and Saccarappa Park agreement.
summary: The council also adopted a 6-1 vote amending the code for the Recreation & Conservation Commission and approved a permit for a Halloween street closure on Main Street. Orders on a Bureau of Highway Safety grant and a drainage easement at 41 Brown Street were approved on the first of two readings. Mayor Morse also gave updates on brush and leaf collection.
decisions: Approved Orders 2026-109 through 2026-112 and 2026-114 on second and final reading, 7-0.
Amended Order 2026-113 to include an updated project vendor list, 7-0.
Approved Order 2026-113, a task order with Credere Associates for Riverwalk North, on second and final reading, 7-0.
Approved Resolve 2026-18 endorsing the city's Community Development Block Grant applications, 7-0.
Approved Order 2026-115 authorizing a memorandum of understanding with Quaker Lane Associates for Saccarappa Park improvements, 7-0.
Approved Order 2026-116 amending the city code on the Recreation & Conservation Commission, 6-1.
Approved Order 2026-117, a mass gathering permit and road closure for Halloween on Main Street, 7-0.
Approved first of two readings of Order 2026-118 on acceptance and spending of Bureau of Highway Safety grant funds, by show of hands with none opposed.
Approved first of two readings of Order 2026-119 authorizing a drainage easement at 41 Brown Street, by show of hands with none opposed.
Approved first of two readings of Order 2026-120 amending the land use ordinance on data centers, by show of hands with none opposed.

plain_text:
WESTBROOK CITY COUNCIL 
SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 
MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026 AT 6:00 PM  
WESTBROOK HIGH SCHOOL (ROOM 114) 
125 STROUDWATER ST.  
 
 
 
  
I. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT 
Meeting called to order at 6:00pm by City Council President Jennifer Munro. President Munro stated a 
reminder of the City Council Rules of Order regarding meeting conduct. City Clerk Ellis Ledoux read the City 
Council Land Acknowledgment statement into the record. 
 
  
II. ROLL CALL 
City Councilors Present: Michael Shaughnessy (At-Large, Vice-President), Brian McCambridge (Ward 1), Anna A. 
Turcotte (Ward 3), Victor Chau (Ward 2), Amy Faulkingham (Ward 4), Jennifer Munro (Ward 5, President), Gary 
Rairdon (At-Large) 
 
City Councilors Absent: None 
 
Other City Officials Present: Eric Dudley (Director of Engineering & Public Services), Jennie Franceschi 
(Assistant City Administrator), Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Bruno Inácio (Finance Director), Sean Lally 
(Police Chief), Ellis Ledoux (City Clerk), David Morse (Mayor), Robyn Saunders (Project Manager), Stephen Sloan 
(Fire Chief), Monqiue Cornett (Director of Economic Development), Rebecca Spitella (Director of Planning & 
Code Enforcement), Cameron Ferrante (Legal Counsel), Gary Wagner (Assistant Fire Chief) 
 
  
III. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
City Council President Munro led all present in the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
  
IV. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
No minutes were presented for approval. 
 
  
V. MAYOR'S MESSAGE  
 
 Mayor Morse read his message into the record. A Summary are included below: 
• The Mayor gave the floor to Chris Chop, Transportation Director for Greater Portland Council 
of Governments (GPCOG) to present on the Route 302 Corridor Study 
• Today marks the first day of brush collection for this season. Mayor Morse invited Eric Dudley 
to the podium to go through the services that Public Services provides during this time. 
Collection will begin next Friday. Leaf collection will start next Monday.  
• Mayor Morse gave the floor to City Clerk Ledoux to provide information on Absentee Voting 
and Election Day
• City Staff will be reviewing our no-parking signage and schedule to ensure that they are in 
alignment. An annual report will be provided to Council moving forward. 
• Prospect Street & Central Street updates  
• William F King Jr. Award was given to Councilor Shaughnessy, recognizing his work with DDW 
and Friends of the Presumpscot River 
• Addressed the use of student photos in the media. Proud of the overwhelming response of the 
community to this incident and standing with our students. 
 
  
VI. CITY COUNCIL MESSAGES 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for City Council messages. Councilors provided the following 
updates: 
• Councilor Chau this last Saturday the Marching Band had a show and competed with other 
communities and states. Thanks to Councilor McCambridge for his help cleaning up after this event. 
The Westbrook Drama Club has a show this Thursday at 7pm. It's free.  
• Councilor Turcotte requested clarification on when the start time of the City Council meetings changed 
from 7pm to 6pm. Note: During the first public comment portion of the meeting, Angela Holmes (City 
Administrator) was able to note that the change in the Council meeting start times was amended with 
Council Order 2024-146. 
 
  
VII. STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE UPDATE 
There was no Student Representative update. 
 
  
VIII. PUBLIC COMMENT 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for the first public comment portion of this meeting. The 
following individuals spoke: David VonSeggern (Resident of Westbrook), Matthew Brunner (Resident of 
Westbrook), Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Councilor Turcotte 
 
  
IX. UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
There was no unfinished business for consideration.  
 
  
X. ORDERS OF THE DAY (SECOND AND FINAL READING)  
 
 Order 2026-109. Authorizing Award of Bid for Replacement Medium-Duty Pick-Up Truck for Fire 
Department  
Order 2026-110. Authorizing Acceptance of Federal Asset Forfeiture Funds 
Order 2026-111. Authorizing Expenditure to Presumpscot Regional Land Trust for Mill Brook 
Preserve Improvements 
Order 2026-112. Authorizing Expenditure for Portland Trails Rock Row Connector Trail 
Order 2026-114. Amending Several Orders Relating to the Landslide Vulnerability Assessment Project 
& Amending Vendor List  
 Motion to approve second and final reading of Orders 2026-109-112, and Order 2026-114 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Vice President Shaughnessy
City Council President Munro asked if any Councilor would like to consider any item separately. Order 
2026-113 to be taken separately.  
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: No one spoke. 
Motion carried. Orders 2026–109 through 2026-112, & 2026-114 adopted. (Vote 7-0) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, McCambridge, Chau, Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
  
 
 Order 2026-113. Authorizing Task Order No. 11 with Credere Associates for Supplemental Services 
Regarding Riverwalk North  
 Motion to amend Order 2026-113 to include an updated project vendor list. 
Moved by Councilor Chau, seconded by Vice President Shaughnessy 
Motion carried. Order 2026-113 amended (Vote 7-0) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, McCambridge, Chau, Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
 
Motion to approve second and final reading of Order 2026-113, as amended 
Moved by Councilor Chau, seconded by Vice President Shaughnessy 
City Council President Munro asked if any Councilor would like to consider any item separately. No one 
spoke 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: No one spoke. 
Motion carried. Order 2026-113 adopted. (Vote 7-0) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, McCambridge, Chau, Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
 
  
XI. NEW BUSINESS  
 
  
 Business Licenses 
 There were no business licenses for consideration 
 
  
 Resolves (One Reading Required)  
 
 Resolve 2026-18. Endorsing the City of Westbrook's Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) 
Applications  
 Motion to approve the first and final reading of the legislation. 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: City Administrator Holmes 
Motion carried. Resolve 2026-18 adopted. (Vote 7-0) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, McCambridge, Chau,Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
 
  
 Orders (One Reading Required)
Order 2026-115. Authorizing Memorandum of Understanding with Quaker Lane Associates, LLC 
Regarding Improvements at Saccarappa Park  
 Motion to approve the first and final reading of the legislation.  
Moved by Councilor Faulkingham, seconded by Vice President Shaughnessy 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator) 
Motion carried. Order 2026-115 adopted. (Vote 7-0) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, McCambridge, Chau, Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
  
 
 Order 2026-116. Amending the Westbrook Code of Ordinances Regarding the Recreation & 
Conservation Commission  
 Motion to approve the first and final reading of the legislation.  
Moved by Vice President Shaughnessy, seconded by Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator), President Munro, Cameron Ferrante (Legal Counsel), 
Rebecca Spitella (Director of Planning & Code Enforcement), Mayor Morse, Councilor Rairdon, 
Councilor McCambridge, Vice President Shaughnessy, Councilor Turcotte (see point of order below) 
 
Point of Order. During Councilor Turcotte's portion of council comment, President Munro called for  
point of order several times to remind Councilor Turcotte to confine her comments to the merits of the 
issue in accordance with City Council's Rules of Order Section 5(A), regarding discussion and use of 
intemperate and abusive language. 
 
Motion carried. Order 2026-116 adopted. (Vote 6-1) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, McCambridge, Chau, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: Turcotte 
  
 
 Order 2026-117. Approving Mass Gathering Permit & Road Closure for Halloween on Main Street  
 Motion to approve the first and final reading of the legislation.  
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Councilor Chau, Councilor Rairdon, Sean Lally (Police Chief) 
Motion carried. Order 2026-117 adopted. (Vote 7-0) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, McCambridge, Chau, Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
 
  
 Orders (Two Readings Required)  
 
 Order 2026-118. Authorizing Acceptance & Expenditure of Bureau of Highway Safety Grant Funds  
 Motion to approve the first of two readings of the legislation. 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator) 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed.
Order 2026-119. Authorizing a Drainage Easement at 41 Brown Street  
 Motion to approve the first of two readings of the legislation. 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, McCambridge 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator) 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed. 
  
 
 Order 2026-120. Amending the Land Use Ordinance Regarding Data Centers  
 Motion to approve the first of two readings of the legislation. 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Councilor McCambridge 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Mayor Morse  
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed. 
 
  
XII. PUBLIC COMMENT 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for the second and final public comment portion of this 
meeting. The following individuals spoke: Chris Dudley (Ward 1, Westbrook Resident) 
 
  
XIII. REFERRALS 
There were no referrals for consideration.  
 
  
XIV. COMMITTEE REPORTS  
 
 The following items remain in their City Council Committees for deliberation. No updates were 
provided by Committee Chairs. 
 
Committee of the Whole 
Board, Commission, Committee Ordinance  
Code of Conduct & Job Descriptions for Elected Officials 
Private Ways Ordinance  
 
Facilities & Streets Committee 
Establishment of Memorial Area 
Policy on Establishing Memorial Areas 
Friends of Warren Recreational Area Introductions & Updates 
Haskell Street Traffic Calming 
 
Housing & Economic Development Committee 
Cannabis Dispensary Zoning Regulations  
  
XV. EXECUTIVE SESSION  
 
 Request to enter into Executive Session pursuant to 1 M.R.S.A. Section 405-6(E) for consultation with 
the City Solicitor concerning the legal rights and duties of the City, inviting the following individuals to
attend: Mayor, City Administrator, Asst. City Administrator, City Clerk, Project Manager, and City 
Solicitor. 
 Motion to enter into Executive Session at 7:45pm as stated above. 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, Councilor Chau 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed.  
 
  
XVI. ADJOURNMENT 
Motion to adjourn directly following executive session at 9:45pm 
Moved by Councilor Chau, seconded by Vice President Shaughnessy 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed.
